pl-l4d8c3-d1e115.summary: Sets four topics to be considered first: institution, form, sacrament, and reality.

pl-l4d8c3-d1e118.summary: States that the Lord instituted the sacrament when, after the typical lamb, he gave his body and blood to the disciples at the Supper.
claims: The eucharist was instituted at the Last Supper.

pl-l4d8c3-d1e121.summary: Quotes Eusebius of Emesa: since he was to take the assumed body from our eyes and bring it to the heavens, it was necessary that on the day of the Supper he consecrate for us the sacrament of his body and blood, so that what was offered once as a price might be honored continually through the mystery.
claims: The eucharist continually honors the sacrifice offered once.

pl-l4d8c3.summary: Sets four topics for the eucharist: institution, form, sacrament, and reality. The Lord instituted it when, after the typical lamb, he gave his body and blood to the disciples at the Supper. Eusebius of Emesa: since he was to take his assumed body from sight, he consecrated the sacrament of his body and blood at the Supper, so that what was offered once as price might be honored continually in mystery.
claims: The eucharist was instituted at the Last Supper after the paschal lamb.
It was instituted so that the sacrifice once offered might be continually honored in mystery.
